newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario police track down escaped Siberian tiger.
newsitem.headline: Ontario police track down escaped Siberian tiger.

text.p: A fugitive Siberian tiger was discovered hiding in the woods near a small Canadian city late on Sunday after roaming free for about 11 hours, forcing residents to cower in their homes.

Police had told people in Barrie and the surrounding area to stay in their houses until they could locate the 600 pound (270 kilogram) tiger which escaped from its new compound about noon EST (1700 GMT).

The four-year-old male tiger, named Zarac, was eventually tracked down in a wooded area behind the Bear Creek Wildlife Sanctuary from which he escaped after being brought there with his mother only the day before, said Sgt. Steve Crowe of the Ontario Provincial Police.
"Apparently the mother tiger has been calling for him," Crowe said. "The idea is that they'll leave him alone and he will go back to mom and be captured humanely."
Police and handlers plan to use chickens to "bait" the tiger back to his cage. Crowe said Zarac scaled a 9-foot (2.7 metre) fence during his jailbreak.

Zarac has been described as having a "timid and shy nature" but police were advising residents near the sanctuary, in Essa Township about one mile (1.6 kilometres) west of Barrie, not to leave their houses until he was safely caged.
Barrie is about 55 miles (90 kilometres) north of Toronto.
